new_statements.rule_in_words: Bure is described as a two-tone language (H, L; falling HL on some syllables), with phonemic vowel length; no accessible source says anything about word stress or accent, neither where it falls nor whether it exists.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement to have exceptions).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement refers to lexical words (nouns, particles); verb tone classes in Batic 2015 are assigned on the first syllable of the perfective plural (p. 102). Stress is not discussed at word or phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the single variety spoken in Bure village (Kirfi LGA, Bauchi State), vernacular name Bùbbúrè, Hausa 'buranci'; no dialect distinctions are reported. Glottocode bure1242 = ISO bvh.
